html:
The Maxakalí, who call themselves Tikmũ'ũn, are an Indigenous people of northeastern Minas Gerais, in Brazil. They speak Maxakalí, of the Maxakalían family, as their first language.

In colonial times their ancestors lived in the Atlantic forest between the Jequitinhonha and Mucuri rivers, one of several small groups that the Portuguese of colonial Brazil often lumped together with the Botocudo. Settlers, cattle ranchers and disease took most of their land in the 1800s and 1900s, and the forest was cleared for pasture. Today about 2,000 people live in a few villages. They are known for a great body of songs tied to spirit beings called yãmĩy. See Brazil.
